title: Communication at the End of Life: A Randomized Intervention to Modify Expectations from a Relatives’ Perspective
summary: Many people avoid conversations about the end of life, with expectations regarding such discussions appearing to play a significant role. This study examines how a brief psychological intervention can help reduce negative expectations and strengthen positive expectations concerning end-of-life conversations. In a preliminary study, a combination of educational reflection and a guided, imagined end-of-life conversation proved effective. The goal of the current study is to determine which of these two components is crucial for success.
conditions: Expectations concerning End-of-Life conversation in the general population

interventions.name: Intervention group "Imagination": Imagined end-of-life conversation with a loved one about their end of life
Intervention group "Educational Reflection": Questions regarding fears and benefits of end-of-life conversations and the provision of research findings on end-of-life conversations
Intervention group "combined": Educational Reflection and Imagination
